prize_parts.citation: for the invention and development of the optical lattice clock, which brought optical frequency measurement to the 10^-18 level of uncertainty

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged from round 1: a single prize part for the optical lattice clock, credited to Hidetoshi Katori and Jun Ye. The round-1 exchange has strengthened my confidence rather than weakened it. The mandate is a discovery or an invention, and this is an invention with an identifiable original step: Katori's magic-wavelength lattice, which removes the trap-induced shift on the clock transition while allowing many atoms to be interrogated at once, and his first strontium lattice clock. Ye's group then demonstrated what the idea could deliver, with uncertainty at the 10^-18 level, millimetre-scale resolution of the gravitational redshift, and the many-body and spin-exchange understanding that explains why the clock reaches that performance. The result is experimentally verified: several independent laboratories have reproduced and surpassed it in Sr, Yb and Hg, and international comparisons are routine. The chair asks whether the citation can rest only on demonstrated results. I think it can, and I have tightened my wording accordingly. It now names the invention and its development, and cites the measured uncertainty, and it leaves out constants, dark matter and the redefinition of the second, which are prospects and not results. The invention and the original experiment are Katori's and Ye's, and I do not see a competing original claim on the lattice idea or on the first realisation at this level. That is the standard I apply when I ask whether we have found the people who did the original work.
statement.case_against: The overlap with the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize is the most serious objection. I do not accept that it is disqualifying, because the comb is the readout and the ion work concerns control of a single quantum system, whereas the lattice clock is a different invention with its own original experiment. But the novelty argument is not trivial, and a reader could still call this a better clock rather than a new phenomenon. No deviation from standard physics has been found, so Danielsson and Eriksson are right that this is a measurement capability and not yet a discovery about nature, and my citation does not pretend otherwise. The pending SI redefinition means the societal payoff is still partly prospective. Finally, the credit boundary around two names does exclude important groups (SYRTE, PTB, NIST, Lemonde, Ludlow, Sterr), and the record on who first established each systematic correction is not fully in front of me.

responses.point: Ranks B008 first, judges the uncertainty budgets credible from her own experience with systematic-shift and atomic-structure calculations, and notes that she is a close reader of the field.
responses.response: In round 1 I asked you whether any key systematic, such as the lattice light shift, blackbody radiation or hyperpolarisability, was first established by a group outside Katori and Ye. You have not yet answered and the chair has put the same question to you. I would like a direct reply, because it decides whether two names are enough. If the magic-wavelength condition and the first demonstration are Katori's, and the decisive reduction to the 10^-18 level is Ye's, then the boundary holds. If an essential correction was first shown elsewhere, I would still keep the pair, but I would then want the citation to say what the invention is and not imply that every element of the clock is theirs. Your close reading of the field does not disqualify you, and I welcome your view on that boundary.

responses.point: Ranks B008 first, discloses a year in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder and the association of Ye with the Hall and JILA group, and says the committee may wish to consider recusal; he also floats a two-part prize pairing B008 with another part.
responses.response: Thank you for disclosing this early. A year in Hall's laboratory during a PhD is a personal connection, but you report no collaboration with Katori or Ye, and I regard it as a field-proximity matter. My view is that you may take part if the disclosure is recorded in the minutes, so long as your argument rests on the evidence. In your own case against you also say the invention could be argued as Katori's alone. I would resist that. Katori gave the idea and the first strontium lattice clock, but the validation of the concept at the level that matters for precision tests came from Ye's group, and the citation should say both. On a two-part configuration I do not support it. The three-person cap makes a split awkward and I would not add a second part only to bring the count of names up.

responses.point: Ranks B049 first as a new state of matter with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, argues that the Z2 theory plus the HgTe observation is a complete core, and names B008 as the cleanest fallback.
responses.response: I take the physics seriously and I accept the maturity and the lasting influence. My concern remains the one I raised in round 1. The HgTe experiment tested the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, not the Kane-Mele graphene model, and I would not want the citation to imply a line that the papers do not support. I notice that you say your own recollection of the Kane-Mele priority is not independently verified, and that is exactly the type of uncertainty I do not want in a prize citation. On your doubt that a measurement capability is weaker than a discovery, I agree that a new state of matter is a stronger type of result, but I do not think that is the right criterion here. What I ask is whether the credited people are the ones who did the original work, and for B008 I can say yes more clearly than for B049. I am glad you call B008 the cleanest fallback.

responses.point: Moved to B049 as the broadest-supported theory-led candidate, and states that he would rather lose the configuration than award it on a distorted record because of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and the 3D story.
responses.response: I respect that you would give up the configuration instead of distorting the record, and I think that is the right instinct for this committee. It is also the reason I keep B049 as an alternative and not as my preferred part: a citation worded around the concept and first observation could be defended, but the lineage from graphene to HgTe to 3D would remain contested within a three-person cap. You also ask whether a technology-heavy candidate should stand on equal footing with a concept-driven one. I would say it can, if it is an original invention that opens measurements nobody could make before, and if the result has been verified independently. I think B008 meets that test, and I would add that you list it as an alternative.

responses.point: Prefers the Higgs discovery (B056) with Gianotti, Jenni and Virdee, but concedes that the choice of three from four is a judgement the record cannot settle and that B008 has the cleaner attribution.
responses.response: I appreciate that you say you would rather lose on attribution than pretend it is easy. I agree on the science: the Higgs discovery is permanent and central. My difficulty is that the Statutes ask us to name individuals who did the original work, and I cannot show from the record why Della Negra should be dropped in favour of the others, or the reverse. Spokesperson roles describe leadership at a point in time. They do not by themselves show who made the discovery possible, and in my opening ballot I myself named a different trio from yours. Until someone offers a rule that the four credited people would each accept, I regard B056 as a strong alternative but not a prize I can be sure is correctly attributed.

responses.point: Moved B008 to first place, notes that no deviation from standard physics has been found, and says the new physics it enables is mostly prospective; he also proposes to recuse himself from B012.
responses.response: Your caution about prospective physics is the reason I changed my citation. I agree that what has been shown is millimetre-scale redshift and the uncertainty budgets, and the committee should say that and no more. Thank you also for the plain statement on B012. I accept your recusal and I do not think B012 should come into the final ballot as more than a distant alternative, given the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits and the missing credit for Girvin and Huard. I would not want my own disclosure on B009 to be treated differently, so I confirm that I will not take part in deciding it.

uncertainties: Whether any essential systematic correction (lattice light shift, blackbody radiation, hyperpolarisability, density shift) was first established by a group outside Katori and Ye. If so, the citation must be worded around the invention and its leading realisation and not around the clock as a whole.

How much weight the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize should carry against the novelty of the lattice clock. I judge that they do not cover the invention, but this is a judgement.

Whether the committee will accept a measurement capability, with no deviation from standard physics yet found, as the type of achievement the mandate describes. I think it does, as long as the citation rests on demonstrated results.
Whether the credit boundary of two names is defensible against SYRTE, PTB, NIST, Lemonde, Ludlow and Sterr. I have not seen evidence that any of them made the original invention.
statement.conflict_note: Updated disclosure. I keep my field-proximity conflict with B009 (spherical-aberration correction in TEM) as an electron microscopist and as President of the IFSM, and I will not take part in deciding that candidate. B009 is not in my preferred configuration or among my alternatives. I have no personal or institutional connection to Katori, Ye or their groups, or to the credited names for B049 and B056. Göran Johansson is a colleague at Chalmers Physics, and Bernhard Mehlig is in the neighbouring Gothenburg department; neither tie bears on B008. I note Stefan Kroll's disclosure on B008 and think it should be recorded, with the committee deciding on his participation.
